task_prompts.click-type--hex-color:
Add a new built-in parameter type to Click: `click.HEX_COLOR`, which accepts a CSS hex color written as `#RGB` or `#RRGGBB` (case-insensitive, the `#` is required) and converts it to the normalized lower-case 6-digit form `#rrggbb` (a `str`). Values it cannot convert must fail with Click's usual "Invalid value" usage error. Examples of valid input: `#FFF`, `#1a2B3c`, `#000000`. Examples of invalid input: `fff`, `#12345`, `#ggg`.

Include tests, document the new type in the API reference and in the parameter types guide, and add a changelog entry.
task_prompts.click-type--port:
Add a new built-in parameter type to Click: `click.PORT`, which accepts a TCP/UDP port number, an integer from 1 to 65535 inclusive, and converts it to an `int`. Values it cannot convert must fail with Click's usual "Invalid value" usage error. Examples of valid input: `80`, `65535`, `1`. Examples of invalid input: `0`, `65536`, `http`.

Include tests, document the new type in the API reference and in the parameter types guide, and add a changelog entry.
task_prompts.click-type--duration:
Add a new built-in parameter type to Click: `click.DURATION`, which accepts a duration written as one or more `<integer><unit>` parts with the units `d`, `h`, `m` and `s`, in that order (for example `1h30m`, `45s`, `2d`), and converts it to a `datetime.timedelta`. Values it cannot convert must fail with Click's usual "Invalid value" usage error. Examples of valid input: `1h30m`, `45s`, `2d`, `1d2h3m4s`. Examples of invalid input: `10`, `1x`, `h`, `30m1h`.

Include tests, document the new type in the API reference and in the parameter types guide, and add a changelog entry.
task_prompts.click-type--ip-address:
Add a new built-in parameter type to Click: `click.IP_ADDRESS`, which accepts an IPv4 or IPv6 address and converts it to an `ipaddress.IPv4Address` or `ipaddress.IPv6Address`. Values it cannot convert must fail with Click's usual "Invalid value" usage error. Examples of valid input: `127.0.0.1`, `::1`, `192.168.1.20`. Examples of invalid input: `256.1.1.1`, `localhost`, `1.2.3`.

Include tests, document the new type in the API reference and in the parameter types guide, and add a changelog entry.
task_prompts.click-type--semver:
Add a new built-in parameter type to Click: `click.SEMVER`, which accepts a semantic version `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` of non-negative integers, optionally prefixed with `v`, and converts it to a tuple of three `int`s. Values it cannot convert must fail with Click's usual "Invalid value" usage error. Examples of valid input: `1.2.3`, `v0.10.0`, `10.0.1`. Examples of invalid input: `1.2`, `1.2.x`, `1.2.3.4`.

Include tests, document the new type in the API reference and in the parameter types guide, and add a changelog entry.
task_prompts.click-type--percentage:
Add a new built-in parameter type to Click: `click.PERCENTAGE`, which accepts a percentage from 0 to 100 inclusive, written with or without a trailing `%` (for example `50%`, `12.5`), and converts it to a `float` fraction (`50%` becomes `0.5`). Values it cannot convert must fail with Click's usual "Invalid value" usage error. Examples of valid input: `50%`, `12.5`, `100%`, `0`. Examples of invalid input: `101%`, `-1`, `abc`.

Include tests, document the new type in the API reference and in the parameter types guide, and add a changelog entry.
task_prompts.click-type--byte-size:
Add a new built-in parameter type to Click: `click.BYTE_SIZE`, which accepts a size in bytes written as a number with an optional unit: `B`, `KB`, `MB`, `GB` (powers of 1000) or `KiB`, `MiB`, `GiB` (powers of 1024), case-insensitive, and converts it to an `int` number of bytes (a bare number is bytes; `1.5MB` is `1500000`). Values it cannot convert must fail with Click's usual "Invalid value" usage error. Examples of valid input: `10KB`, `1KiB`, `512`, `1.5MB`, `2gib`. Examples of invalid input: `10XB`, `-1KB`, `KB`.

Include tests, document the new type in the API reference and in the parameter types guide, and add a changelog entry.
task_prompts.click-type--slug:
Add a new built-in parameter type to Click: `click.SLUG`, which accepts a URL slug: lower-case ASCII letters and digits in groups separated by single hyphens (for example `my-post-2`), and returns it unchanged as a `str`. Values it cannot convert must fail with Click's usual "Invalid value" usage error. Examples of valid input: `my-post-2`, `abc`, `a1-b2`. Examples of invalid input: `Hello`, `a--b`, `-a`, `a_b`.

Include tests, document the new type in the API reference and in the parameter types guide, and add a changelog entry.
task_prompts.click-type--date:
Add a new built-in parameter type to Click: `click.DATE`, which accepts a calendar date in ISO format `YYYY-MM-DD` and converts it to a `datetime.date`. Values it cannot convert must fail with Click's usual "Invalid value" usage error. Examples of valid input: `2024-02-29`, `1999-12-31`. Examples of invalid input: `2024-13-01`, `01/02/2024`, `2023-02-29`.

Include tests, document the new type in the API reference and in the parameter types guide, and add a changelog entry.
task_prompts.click-type--host-port:
Add a new built-in parameter type to Click: `click.HOST_PORT`, which accepts a `host:port` pair (a non-empty host name and a port from 1 to 65535) and converts it to a tuple `(host, port)` of a `str` and an `int`. Values it cannot convert must fail with Click's usual "Invalid value" usage error. Examples of valid input: `localhost:8080`, `example.com:443`. Examples of invalid input: `localhost`, `host:0`, `:80`, `host:http`.
